brand_names: Certain Dri Clinical Strength Prescription Protection Roll-On
what_its_for: This is a strong antiperspirant that helps control excessive sweating (hyperhidrosis). It works by temporarily blocking your sweat glands to reduce the amount of sweat your body produces, especially in the underarm area.
how_to_take: Apply this roll-on only to your underarm skin. Make sure your underarms are completely dry before applying — it works best when applied to dry skin. Roll on a thin, even layer. Do not rub it in. Let it dry completely before getting dressed. For best results, apply at bedtime before you go to sleep, since sweat glands are less active at night. In the morning, you may shower or bathe as usual — the product will still be working even after you wash.
dosing: Apply once daily at bedtime to each dry underarm. Once your sweating is under control, you may be able to reduce how often you apply it — for example, just 2 or 3 times per week. Follow the directions on your product label or as your doctor recommends.
missed_dose: This product is applied as needed rather than on a strict schedule. If you forget to apply it one night, simply apply it the next time you remember at bedtime. Do not apply a double amount to make up for a missed application.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 59°F and 77°F (15°C and 25°C). Keep the cap tightly closed when not in use. Keep away from open flames, heat, and sparks — this product is flammable. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Do not apply to broken, irritated, or recently shaved skin, as this can cause burning or stinging. Wait at least 24 to 48 hours after shaving before applying. Do not apply near your eyes or mouth. Do not use on any body area other than your underarms unless directed by your doctor. Avoid applying right after a shower or bath when skin is still damp — always make sure skin is fully dry first. Do not use near an open flame or while smoking.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or stop using this product if you notice: severe skin redness, rash, or blistering; intense burning or stinging that does not go away; signs of a skin infection such as warmth, swelling, or oozing; or if your sweating does not improve after several weeks of regular use. Also contact your doctor if you develop a rash or allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing.
when_it_works: You may start to notice less sweating within the first few days of nightly use. Most people see the best results after 1 to 2 weeks of consistent use. Once your sweating is well controlled, you can usually maintain results by applying it just a few times per week.
special_populations: Children under 12 years of age: Do not use unless directed by a doctor. Pregnant or breastfeeding women: Talk to your doctor before using this product. Elderly patients: No special precautions are generally needed, but check with your doctor if you have sensitive skin or any skin conditions.
